placements.alt: Three cards in a row: Context leads to Task, and Task to Decision.
Four cards in a row: Know, Act, Check, and Stop.
A card listing typical cases, edge cases, and must refuse leads to a card marked Evaluate and ship, each line checked.
Three cards in a row: Research, Onboarding, and Redesign.
Diagram: cards for Fleet, Hours, and Orders feed an Assign load card that lists its evidence, with Approve and Change buttons; the final call stays with the dispatcher.
Diagram: Plan, Build, Test, and Ship each pass a technical check, while User task completion below them is still marked Needs validation.
Diagram: a questionable pair of primary buttons in the design system becomes a written rule, then an automated check; the definition of done still keeps a designer review.
Diagram: Model, Retrieval, Connections, and Skills feed an agent loop of Plan, Act, and Check; at the boundary the run pauses for a person to approve or stop it.
Diagram: an agent reports an invoice as Paid; checked against records, it was Issued, but not yet Charged or Matched.
Diagram: context and constraints feed an agent, whose work passes Draft, Review, Repair, and Approve, with judgment at Review and Approve.
Diagram: the product problem and success measure feed an evaluation plan of typical, edge, and refusal cases, agreed before prompting.
A requirements card with nine identical fields, every one asked for at once.
A requirements card with three sections, the evaluation plan marked as the one this risk calls for.
Diagram: a five-day sprint with an autonomy boundary, where the AI may draft and suggest and people send and commit, and a Friday test with one answer wrong on purpose.
Diagram: a grid of answers stops at a line marked Stop gathering, then synthesis narrows them to three findings and one decision.
Answer cards scattered and overlapping, with one more arriving.
The same answer cards in three straight columns, joined into one finding.
Diagram: past interviews with known answers on one side of an evidence boundary, and sessions observing people today, with one new behavior, on the other.
Diagram: three answers, budget, time, and equipment, shape a first meal plan that is ready right away.
Diagram: a crowded CRM narrows in three steps, cut, rethink, and refine, to one follow-up with a Send button; polish comes last.
